_about: Community questions for waterbodies. Type questions set the fields that the type rules read (inflow, ownership; types.json) so that the type, and every rule that depends on it, is recomputed. Stress questions carry likelihood ratios (lr) for the rules in rules.json, as in the watershed atlas: the data result sets a prior, each answer multiplies the odds. 'rules' lists the rules a stress question informs; 'applies_to' the types a type question is asked for.

assessment.about: The data result for a rule sets a prior probability that the stress or opportunity is present: higher when it triggered and with higher intensity, pulled toward 50% for lower-confidence rules. Each answer multiplies the odds by its likelihood ratio for that rule. A rule counts as present at positive_at or more.
assessment.partial_rule: Triggered: prior = triggered_min + (triggered_max − triggered_min) × intensity/100. Not triggered: prior = not_triggered + (partial_max − not_triggered) × intensity/100, so partial evidence starts higher. Unknown: 0.4.
assessment.shrink_rule: prior = 0.5 + (base_prior - 0.5) × shrink. A low-confidence rule's data result is held less firmly, so answers move it further.
assessment.severity_rule: A positive rule is severe when the data say severe (intensity at or above the rule's severe_at) and the answers have not lowered its probability, or when an answer marked severe was given and the probability is at least severe_at.
assessment.unknown_rule: A rule with missing data starts just below the positive line (0.4), so it is not counted as present until an answer supports it.

type_questions.text: Who owns this waterbody, and who uses its water?
type_questions.rationale: The data cannot tell a farm pond from a small village pond; the census records ownership (public or private) for every waterbody. A private pond is a farm pond whatever its size; a common pond is a village pond unless it is fed by a stream.
type_questions.origin: New; follows the Water Body Census ownership field

options.label: One farmer or family, on their own land
The village, panchayat or a government department; several families use it

type_questions.text: In the monsoon, where does most of its water come from?
type_questions.rationale: Whether a stream or nala feeds the waterbody decides between an on-stream tank, a headwater pond and a pond filled by runoff from fields; the mapped drainage lines miss small channels and canal feeders.

options.label: A stream or nala flows into it, or it is held by a bund or check dam across one
Rain running off the surrounding fields and slopes; no stream
A canal or a channel from a larger tank fills it

stress_questions.text: Are the channels that bring water into this waterbody working, or are they blocked, broken or cut off?
stress_questions.rationale: Poor filling with an ample catchment usually means the supply channels are silted, broken or cut by roads and fields; a sudden loss can follow a blocked inlet.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the inflow shortfall rule

options.label: They work; water flows in freely
Blocked or cut off by a road, field, wall or another structure

stress_questions.text: Has runoff that used to reach it been diverted upstream, by new fields, roads, check dams or other ponds?
stress_questions.rationale: New structures upstream capture runoff that used to reach older tanks, a common cause of poor filling in intensively treated watersheds.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the inflow shortfall rule

options.label: Some, by a few new structures or fields
A lot; little water reaches it now

stress_questions.text: How much silt has built up since it was last desilted?
stress_questions.rationale: Silt reduces storage both as a falling trend (siltation) and, where it built up before 2017, as poor filling. The census records storage lost to silt for many tanks.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the siltation and inflow rules

options.label: Little; it was desilted in the last few years
Noticeable; it is shallower than before
A lot; much of the bed has filled up

stress_questions.text: Is part of the bed or its edges being farmed or built on?
stress_questions.rationale: Encroachment shrinks the water spread; in the census comparison, encroached waterbodies triggered siltation more often (32% against 21%).
stress_questions.origin: New; from the siltation rule and the census comparison

options.label: A large part, or it has been drained for fields or building

stress_questions.text: Does water leak out through the sluice, outlet or bund?
stress_questions.rationale: Early drying with a full monsoon fill points to leaking sluices and bunds, or to heavy drawal; a breach shows as a sudden loss.

options.label: The sluice or outlet is damaged

stress_questions.text: In a normal year, until when does it hold water?
stress_questions.rationale: How long water lasts decides rabi irrigation, summer water for animals and whether a fish crop (4 to 6 months) is possible; satellite extent can miss shallow water or count wet mud.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the retention, livestock and fishery rules

options.label: Through the summer, or all year

stress_questions.text: In the last drought year, could farmers take water from it to save the kharif crop?
stress_questions.rationale: A tank's main value in semi-arid areas is protective irrigation in dry spells; if it fails exactly then, deepening and catchment work are the remedy.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the drought failure rule

options.label: Yes, enough for most fields that needed it
A little, for a few fields

stress_questions.text: How was its water shared in the last dry season?
stress_questions.rationale: Agreed sharing rules spread the benefit of stored water; their absence is a common reason why water stays unused or goes to a few.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the drought and irrigation rules

options.label: First come, or by those with pumps or influence

stress_questions.text: How many of the fields below or around it are irrigated from it in rabi?
stress_questions.rationale: Water that lasts into rabi with little second-season cropping around it may be unused; the answer separates unused water from cropping limited by other factors.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the irrigation underuse rule

stress_questions.text: Is there a water user association or committee for this waterbody?
stress_questions.rationale: In the census comparison, waterbodies with a water user association triggered irrigation underuse half as often (19% against 40%).

options.label: Yes, and it meets and sets rules

stress_questions.text: Are the field channels and outlets from it working?
stress_questions.rationale: Broken field channels are the most direct reason why stored water does not reach fields.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the irrigation underuse rule

stress_questions.text: Where do animals drink in April to June?
stress_questions.rationale: Where animals are walked far or water is carried, a pond that dries before summer is a real loss.

options.label: Troughs filled from a borewell or tanker
They are taken far, or water is carried

stress_questions.text: Is it used for fishing now, and who holds the rights?
stress_questions.rationale: A waterbody that lasts into rabi where villages fish is a candidate for stocking; unclear rights or pollution make it unsuitable.

options.label: Yes, by a group or cooperative under a lease
Not now, but people want to
No: it dries early, is polluted, or the rights are disputed

stress_questions.text: Does fishing stop early because the water dries up?
stress_questions.rationale: Carp need a culture period of several months; ponds that dry by rabi cut it short.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the fishery constraint rule

stress_questions.text: In the last rabi season, did canal water reach this waterbody when it was needed?
stress_questions.rationale: Tail-end tanks of canal systems get water late or not at all; the answer separates canal supply from local losses.
stress_questions.origin: New; from the canal tail rule

stress_questions.text: Does the river here dry up earlier in summer than it did ten years ago?
stress_questions.rationale: Earlier drying of a river reach follows falling base flow, from pumping near the river and catchment change.

options.label: Much earlier; it is now dry by March or April

stress_questions.text: Is sand mined from this stretch of the river?
stress_questions.rationale: Sand mining lowers the bed and the water table beside it and speeds up drying.

options.label: With machines or on a large scale
